title: Emrys and the Verdict
premise: Jonah Okafor, the meticulous archivist of St. Brannoc's Cathedral, discovers that the diary of Maren Voss—a woman who vanished thirty years ago—contains entries written after her disappearance, in handwriting that is unmistakably hers. As Jonah and the cathedral's ragtag found family of misfits investigate, they uncover that the crypt's lock was changed the very week Maren vanished, and that several of the town's most respected elders wove their alibis together like a net. The trail leads to a living Maren, hidden for decades by those who loved her and by one who wanted her silenced, and to the truth that her 'disappearance' was an escape from a crime she witnessed. In the end Jonah must choose between protecting the fragile found family that sheltered her and exposing the truth—the verdict rendered not by a court, but by what Jonah files in the archive for the town to finally read.
about_author: P. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was supposed to read twice. They write mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside institutions, from a house full of rescued greyhounds.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Jonah Okafor's POV. A routine donation of papers to the cathedral archive includes a water-stained diary belonging to Maren Voss, missing since 1994. Jonah catalogs it out of habit, noting the final dated entry. Emotional beat: the comfort of order, faintly disturbed by something that doesn't fit the system.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Reading late at night, Jonah realizes the diary continues three weeks past the date Maren disappeared—and describes the crypt itself. The last entry names a place: 'the third door.' Emotional beat: dread blooming inside routine; the archive suddenly feels like a mouth.

chapters.title: The Third Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Behind a false panel in the crypt wall, Jonah finds a bundle: photographs, a key, and a second diary half-burned. Someone has been in this space recently—the dust is disturbed. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear; Jonah is standing where a missing woman stood.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Deacon Ruth Ellery, the bell-ringer Silas, and teenage volunteer Priya. Jonah shows them the find over burnt toast in the vestry; each reacts differently—Ruth wants it reported, Silas goes pale, Priya wants to solve it. Emotional beat: warmth of the group tested by its first real fracture.

chapters.title: What Silas Knew
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, 1994 flashbacks braided into present. He remembers Maren, remembers the night the crypt lock was changed, and remembers being paid to forget by whom he won't say. Emotional beat: guilt as a stone carried so long it has become part of his body.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing old parish registers, Jonah maps the alibis: five townspeople, five identical stories, all placing each other at the harvest fete the night Maren vanished. Too neat. Emotional beat: the archivist's thrill of pattern recognition turning to horror at what the pattern says.

chapters.title: The Verger's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Sneaking into the verger's office, Priya finds a ledger with pages razored out—but carbon copies survive in the duplicate book. Payments. Monthly, for thirty years, to someone initialled only 'M.V.' Emotional beat: righteous excitement shadowed by the first real danger.

chapters.title: Someone Is Filing Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The archive has been searched; folders re-shelved millimeters off. Then a note appears in Jonah's own filing system, in Jonah's own classification code: STOP. Only someone who knows the archive intimately could have done it. Emotional beat: violation; the sanctuary inverted into a trap.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Deacon Ruth's POV. She admits she knew Maren—they were close, closer than the town ever guessed—and that she helped her disappear. But she swears Maren left alive. She has been receiving letters signed M. every year since. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as its own kind of secret-keeping.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ruth produces thirty years of postmarked letters. Handwriting analysis against the diaries: the early ones are Maren's. The last three are not. Someone else knows Maren is alive—and is writing to keep Ruth quiet, or hopeful. Emotional beat: hope weaponized; grief for a friendship built on forged paper.

chapters.title: Harvest Fete, Reprised
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Jonah interviews the surviving four alibi-witnesses under innocuous pretexts. Their stories hold perfectly—until one, Councilman Aldous Pike, slips on a detail that exists only in the diary. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; the hunter realizing he is hunted.

chapters.title: Threats in Triplicate
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya is followed home; Silas's cottage window is broken; the diaries vanish from the archive safe—then reappear, one page missing. The page described the third door's key. Emotional beat: fear tightening around the found family like a fist.

chapters.title: The Key That Fits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The key from the crypt bundle opens a railway locker in the neighboring town containing Maren's real account: she saw Aldous Pike kill a man over land deeds and fled rather than testify, believing no one would believe a caretaker's daughter. Emotional beat: vindication and fury; truth recovered but still powerless.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed Gone
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth explains: Maren chose silence to protect her younger brother, whom Pike threatened. Every year she nearly came back; every year the letters—forged after year ten—kept her tethered and afraid. Emotional beat: sorrowful understanding; the cost of protection measured in decades.

chapters.title: Silas Breaks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Confronted, Silas confesses he was Pike's lookout the night of the murder—not complicit in killing, but paid to swear the fete alibi. He gives Jonah the name of the man Pike killed: the cathedral's former verger. Emotional beat: collapse and release; a burden set down too late to be light.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Reconstructing the torn page from carbon impressions, Jonah finds Maren's plan to return this autumn—the anniversary—for one public reckoning. Pike intercepted the diary to learn when and where. The date is next Sunday: the patronal feast, the whole town present. Emotional beat: countdown dread; the archive becomes a battlefield map.

chapters.title: Choosing Sides
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The found family argues: report to police (who include Pike's nephew) or act alone. Ruth wants to spirit Maren away again; Priya wants exposure; Silas wants penance. Jonah must decide what the archive is for. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—loyalty pulling one way, truth the other.

chapters.title: Feast Day
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The patronal feast unfolds in full ceremonial splendor while Jonah watches the doors, the crowd, the shadows. Pike arrives early and stays late. A gray-haired woman lights a candle at the crypt stair. Emotional beat: held breath; everything ordinary made ominous.

chapters.title: The Crypt Confrontation
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Maren descends to the third door; Pike follows; Jonah locks them both in with the evidence laid out like a court record and reads the reconstructed page aloud through the door. Silas and Ruth bar the exit until the police—called past the nephew—arrive. Emotional beat: climax; quiet words as weapons, the archive as witness stand.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Pike confesses on tape; the nephew recuses himself; charges proceed. Maren, legally dead for thirty years, faces the strange bureaucracy of returning to life. She asks Jonah one question: what will you file? Emotional beat: catharsis; justice arriving small, procedural, and real.

chapters.title: Recataloguing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, Jonah re-catalogues the collection, creating a new finding aid titled 'Voss, M.—Restored.' Some things stay sealed at Maren's request; others go public. Silas tends the bells again; Priya is promoted; Ruth and Maren sit together in the pew. Emotional beat: bittersweet repair; order restored but humbler.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, closing the frame. She visits the crypt one last time, leaves the diaries willingly in Jonah's care, and walks out through the third door left deliberately unlocked. Final line echoes the diary's first entry. Emotional beat: release; memory transformed from burden into inheritance.
